description: A Director of Engineering must approve the initial production rollout policy for an automated dependency-upgrade bot across the engineering organization, including its concurrency limit, approval workflow, and license guardrails, after a cross-functional readiness review.

shared_context.S1: The dependency-upgrade bot has completed its trial on two repositories without producing a failed build.
shared_context.S2: The bot can open pull requests automatically against repositories in the engineering organization.
shared_context.S3: Riley has authority to approve the production rollout policy.
shared_context.S4: The engineering organization uses a final build, security, and operations checklist before enabling a new automation across repositories.

PF1.text: While investigating an unrelated CI queue delay this morning, Mateo confirmed that each dependency-upgrade pull request consumes two shared runner slots and that the organization has 20 slots total; to preserve four slots for ordinary developer builds, the bot must have no more than eight open pull requests at once. He has not updated the rollout proposal yet.

PF2.text: Aisha received legal's confirmed license decision during a security review an hour ago: the bot may merge dependencies under MIT, BSD-2-Clause, or Apache-2.0, but any other license must be blocked and any copyleft dependency must receive manual security review. She has not added the decision to the bot configuration ticket yet.

acceptance_conditions: The bot must begin with a limited production pilot.
The bot must be capped at exactly eight open pull requests.
Human approval must be required before any automated merge.
Only MIT, BSD-2-Clause, and Apache-2.0 dependencies may be merged automatically; other licenses must be blocked and copyleft dependencies must receive manual security review.
A CI-capacity commitment documenting the eight-pull-request limit must be recorded.
A license-review commitment documenting the approved licenses and copyleft review must be recorded.
Mateo's runner-capacity finding must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C4: decisions['license_policy'] == 'allow: MIT,BSD-2-Clause,Apache-2.0; block: all others; manual_review: copyleft'

decisive_facts.why: The bot's open-pull-request limit changes from an unspecified cautious default to exactly eight, and the rollout must record a CI-capacity guardrail because 16 of 20 runner slots would otherwise be consumed.

The automated-merge license policy changes from a generic dependency check to the exact MIT, BSD-2-Clause, and Apache-2.0 allowlist with blocking for all other licenses and manual review for copyleft.
